trickyParts: Relay and hub generations: start and stop under one mutex; a stopped generation publishes only into its own subscriber-less stream; Add on the WaitGroup only while not closed (event_stream_relay.go, delivery_live_hub.go).

The SSE live loop dedupes on one rising id; an overflowed subscription re-subscribes before cancelling the old one and catches up within the replay bounds, while a generation end (reset, test hook, shutdown) still ends the response so the browser reconnects.

Pending comment_deliveries rows are inserted in the comment's transaction with claimed_at null so a queued send left at SIGTERM is recoverable; the sender claims them with claimCommentDeliveryAttempt(initial=true).

A timed-out mention lookup carries no suppression, except that a route string equal to the timed-out mention's target suppresses the route copy (architect's decision); differing strings resolving to one session get two copies (tests pin both).

The delivery hub records what each event touched while a view's read is in flight and re-checks it against the installed answer, so an event during a read is not lost and an unrelated session write causes no second recompute.
deviations: The restart scenario (T1) is built on legion/INFRA-589 and attached as dispatch://INFRA-606/artifact/infra606-restart-scenario-patch; it lands in this PR in the next implementing round, after INFRA-589 merges (architect's decision A, Envoy 2026-10-27T14:03Z), with at least five runs per side per step.
The plan's expectation that Dispatch CPU in the minute after the restart falls below base was not observed beyond run-to-run noise at two runs per side; recorded as measured in the PR body.
Added beyond the plan: the spec's API-3 line (an overflowed SSE subscriber is caught up from the database instead of closed) and a hub race fix (an event during a view's read).
X-Dispatch-Event-Replay: complete is set by this PR server-side (INFRA-492's client reads it); INFRA-492's architect was told the rule over Envoy.
Mention lookups are bounded at 250 ms (architect's amendment) and the issue-route lookup in the comment request uses the same bound.
No partial index for the recovery pass's comment_deliveries query: it runs once per process start (and after a queue overflow drains); a new migration would collide with main's numbering.
